because.label: Committed
because.value: Guaranteed salary already on the books for that season, summed from every contract, including money still owed to players who were traded or released. It is not a payroll projection: arbitration raises and yet-to-be-signed players are not in it, which is why future seasons look so light. What pre-arbitration renewals and arbitration seasons could cost is shown beside it, most likely with the range it could be, never added to it.

because.label: Room
because.value: Budget minus committed salary. OOTP never publishes a future budget (the owner does not set one until the offseason), so seasons after this one assume today's budget holds flat unless you enter what you expect. Either way, treat the later years as a shape, not a forecast.

because.label: Beside each season
because.value: What the seasons the club still controls could cost where no contract covers them yet: pre-arbitration renewals and arbitration years. "Most likely" adds up each player's most likely cost; where a season could go more than one way (which status, which arbitration year, whether he stays) it is a range, from the lowest way to the highest. "Could be" is a range of reasonable readings for the club, not a forecast: players combined as independent; not a calibrated interval. Each player's distance from his most likely cost is combined as independent across players, so not every player lands at his high or low end at once; what isn't chance (a status still open, a range of arbitration years, a player who may leave) stays at its ends, added, and a player who may leave adds nothing to the low end. Each player's own range is a range of reasonable readings, edge against edge (every component at its low edge, every component at its high edge): not an interval with a stated chance, and not an expectation, never narrowed. Not committed, and never in the total or the room.

price.text: What a win costs here isn't known

because.label: What it is
because.value: Opening: the imported market. What clubs in this league pay above the minimum salary for each win a player adds, read from 0 market contracts: most likely, with the range it could be.

because.label: A floor under it
because.value: Across every major leaguer, including those paid below the market by rule, a win costs less: $5.61M. Every major leaguer's pay above the minimum over WAR: a floor, because pay held below the market by rule is in it.

because.label: How it is measured
because.value: Salary above the league minimum ÷ WAR, over 0 market contracts.

because.label: The market
because.value: A market contract is one whose holder Player Rights finds free-agency eligible this season (service at the last winter, when the salary was set). What "the market" is taken to mean is a decision (PLAYER_VALUE.md 4.1, Part 11), not a fit.

because.label: Most likely
because.value: The central value is the median of the market bases that could be computed. R-5 prefers none of them, so none is chosen; the median is the reading that leans on no single one.

because.label: The range
because.value: The band runs from the lowest to the highest market basis that could be computed: the spread of defensible bases, not a statistical interval (R-5). One reading is not a band.

because.label: The floor
because.value: The floor divides every major leaguer's pay above the minimum by his WAR (A), and by the league's WAR (A2). Pre-arbitration and arbitration pay is held below the market by rule, so it understates what a win costs on the open market.

because.label: A
because.value: Every major leaguer on the league's active or injured lists, 2039 WAR: $5.61M

because.label: A2
because.value: The same salaries, over the league's whole 2039 WAR: $5.61M

because.label: B
because.value: Free-agency eligible this season, 2039 WAR: unknown (No player in this population has the salary this basis needs.)

because.label: B2

because.label: B3

because.label: C

because.label: C2

because.label: C3

because.label: When it narrows
because.value: Only observed signings across imports narrow it: a measured price replaces this one when its band is narrower (owner Q-4, phase 4). Nothing in a single import narrows it.

because.label: Which price is in force
because.value: The opening price stays: No off-season observed yet: the measured price needs two imports across a winter (one before its signings and one after). This save has no import recorded yet: its contracts are recorded at each import from now on.

because.label: Measured
because.value: No off-season observed yet: the measured price needs two imports across a winter (one before its signings and one after). This save has no import recorded yet: its contracts are recorded at each import from now on.

because.label: The rule
because.value: The measured price replaces the opening one only when its band is narrower than the opening band with its sampling (owner Q-4): the evidence decides, not a count of signings. The measured price is per win produced in the first season (owner, 2026-09-24: the opening's own unit), its central and band that reading's alone; the readings per win projected at signing are its check on the projection, never the price. It is compared only when its signings cover each third of the winter's free-agent class (review 2026-09-24, a tightening): a winter of cheap deals alone never sets the price.

because.label: Imports kept
because.value: Full contract snapshots are kept for the imports that bracket a winter and the most recent import (owner, 2026-09-24): 0 of 0 imports kept, 0 pruned; every pair of imports observed is kept as stored.

unknown: No contract is a market price: no player on the league's rosters is free-agency eligible (a reserve clause, or nobody has the service). Value is in wins, and dollars are unknown.

costs.text: What a season the club controls costs: a renewal costs $700K to $11.8M (30 renewals this season) · no arbitration contracts on this save to read an arbitration year from yet

because.label: A renewal
because.value: A pre-arbitration renewal: measured on this save. Measured on this save's 30 pre-arbitration renewals (6 at the minimum): $0.70M to $11.81M, central $2.05M (the median renewal); the high edge is the largest of the 30 renewals: too few for the upper bound of their 90th percentile to leave any out, so one renewal sets it.

because.label: An arbitration year
because.value: not known. The export has no WAR for the league in 2038, a platform season.

because.label: Year 1
because.value: not known. Arbitration class 1: not established. The export has no WAR for the league in 2038, a platform season.

because.label: Year 2
because.value: not known. Arbitration class 2: not established. The export has no WAR for the league in 2038, a platform season.

because.label: Year 3
because.value: not known. Arbitration class 3: not established. The export has no WAR for the league in 2038, a platform season.

because.label: The range
because.value: Every band is a range of reasonable readings: each edge takes every component at its own edge (the production band, the class's spread, the line's error, and the price band where the prior is read), edge against edge. It is not an interval with a stated chance, and not an expectation: the central is the reading at the centre of each component.

because.label: Renewals
because.value: A pre-arbitration renewal costs from the league minimum to the 90% upper confidence bound of the 90th percentile of the save's own pre-arbitration one-year renewals this season (Player Rights' pre-arbitration answer), measured at each import; its central is the median renewal. That bound is one of the renewals themselves: below 38 renewals it is the largest, so one unusual renewal can set it; from 38 it leaves the largest out. Below 30 renewals, the provisional prior widened by the save's own renewals where the regime as read is MLB's.

because.label: Arbitration
because.value: An arbitration season costs the league minimum plus its class's line at the platform: a base (the class's pay at no platform wins) and a pay per platform win, against the mean WAR of the 2 seasons before the arbitration winter (the platform season and the one before it), each on its schedule's footing; a season with no line counts 0. The line is read robustly (Theil–Sen: the median of the slopes between every two contracts), so one star or one market contract in the class cannot move it far. The class's spread is the 10th to 90th percentile of its pay around the line, widened by about 1.3 of the line's own standard errors (from 200 bootstrap refits of the same line); never below the least the class was paid above the minimum, except that where the save shows one-year contracts in the class at the league minimum, a season whose platform reaches as low as theirs reaches the minimum too. Read on this import's one-year contracts of players Player Rights finds in arbitration, by class (the class his service puts him in); a contract at the league minimum is kept out of the line (pay there is held at the floor, not set by the platform). Below 30 contracts a class has no line of its own: it is the provisional prior's line, widened by the range the save paid the class, only where the regime as read is MLB's.

because.label: Reserve clause
because.value: A reserve-clause renewal is not priced from one import: it is measured from the renewals observed across imports once enough are seen (phase 4b), and is unknown until then.

because.label: Observed arbitration salaries
because.value: No arbitration salary observed across a winter yet: the ladder is measured on each import and not yet tested against one. The price of a win is unknown, so no observed award is read as a class line (its rung is a share of the price).
